dispositions.reason: Two clauses, neither obligation-bearing. (i) 'Any breach by a Party's Affiliate ... SHALL BE DEEMED a breach by such Party' -- copular legal-fiction statement whose subject is an EVENT, E08-046's 'shall be deemed' precedent. (ii) 'and the other Party may proceed directly against such Party without any obligation to first proceed against such Party's Affiliate' -- a remedies reservation with no standard, no deadline and no required act toward anyone; its only procedural content is a NEGATED precondition. §2.5.1's negative worked example (C14-044 S1, retracted after locking) governs: scope restriction is not monitorable stakes. NOT C13-03, which was annotated because it carries BOTH an explicit gating condition (insolvency) AND a required act toward the counterparty (written notice).
dispositions.span_text: Any breach by a Party’s Affiliate of any of such Party’s obligations under this Supply Agreement shall be deemed a breach by such Party, and the other Party may proceed directly against such Party without any obligation to first proceed against such Party’s Affiliate.

observations.label: INSTANCE ONE -- §3.2's modality table does not cover a present-tense performative ruled obligation-bearing
observations.note:
INSTANCE ONE of a possible §3.2 coverage gap: a PRESENT-TENSE PERFORMATIVE that IS obligation-bearing has no row in §3.2's modality table.

WHAT HAPPENED. The reviewer ruled 2026-09-20 that 'Each Party hereby guarantees...' is obligation-bearing (Reading B; see item E03-03's notes for the full ground). That ruling creates a construction §3.2 does not enumerate. Every row of §3.2's table is a modal verb (shall, must, will, may, should) or a modal-equivalent phrase (agrees to, is required to). 'Hereby guarantees' is neither. §3.2.1's own text calls the table 'exhaustive of what maps to each of the four values'.

WHY IT DID NOT ESCALATE. §3.3 forbids an accept-set for modality, so exactly one value must be chosen, and only MUST is defensible -- the clause creates a binding undertaking and 'agrees to -> MUST' is the nearest row in spirit. MAY, SHOULD and MUST_NOT are all clearly wrong. Unlike the item's EXISTENCE question, which had two defensible answers and did escalate, this has one.

WHY IT IS WORTH A NOTE ANYWAY. Until this ruling, every present-tense performative in the gold set was EXCLUDED by §3.2.1, so the table's silence never mattered -- the question could not arise. Reading B opens the class: a performative that survives §3.2.1's rationale is obligation-bearing and must be assigned a modality by a table that does not describe it. The candidate amendment is a small one -- a §3.2 row or a §3.2.1 cross-reference stating that a performative ruled obligation-bearing takes MUST -- and it is deliberately NOT proposed on one instance, the same discipline §22.1 applies to ruling a kind on a sample of one and the same posture taken for the temporal_composition gap at C04-051 / C04-072.

FOR THE FUTURE SESSION: cite this as INSTANCE ONE. A second present-tense-performative clause ruled obligation-bearing is the forcing function. SEARCH KEY: present-tense performative, hereby guarantees, §3.2 modality table coverage, E03-057, E03-03.
